analyst_view.overall: Inter (15th, 6 points) and Stuttgart (14th, 7 points) meet with both trying to climb into the top eight; Italian press calls it a must-win for Inter, who still face Dortmund and Liverpool. Inter's forwards are coming back: Lautaro Martínez is fit again after a hamstring injury and Thuram is playing, though Bonny (thigh strain, about a month) is out and the numbers don't list him. The numbers already assume Hakan Çalhanoglu is banned for his third yellow (about −7% on Inter's goals); I could not find a press report on the ban either way. Stuttgart's key midfielder Angelo Stiller has missed three games with an adductor injury and is a late doubt; Deniz Undav should lead the line. Inter play at Atalanta on Sunday and Stuttgart played Schalke on Saturday; no referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals and already take 7% off Inter for Çalhanoglu's ban. Bonny being out is balanced by Lautaro coming back after a month out, which the numbers' recent-form figure partly missed. Stiller may miss Stuttgart's game, but he has been out for three games already, so that is in their recent form. Nothing tips it, so I stay at 3.3.

corners.text: The numbers expect 10.1 corners, 6.2 of them Inter's, already up about 5% for Inter's recent corner count. Inter's wing-backs (Dimarco, Spence) are all fit and Stuttgart press high, which fits the usual picture, so I stay at 10.

cards.text: The numbers expect 3.9 cards. The referee is not named yet; Stuttgart's pressing game produces some fouls and the numbers already take a little off them for recent cards. There is no rivalry here and I found nothing new, so I stay at about 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.3 shots and already add 12% to Inter's side for their recent shooting. Inter at home needing a win should shoot plenty, but that is already in the numbers, and Stuttgart's pressing side keeps shooting too. I stay at 31.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target. Lautaro back sharpens Inter's finishing while Bonny's absence takes a forward away, and Undav leads Stuttgart's line as expected. Nothing clearly moves the number, so I stay at 10.
